THR.Settings.ModuleEnabled.Name: Enable Tricky Homebrew Rules
THR.Settings.ModuleEnabled.Hint: Master switch for this world. When off, every rule below is inactive regardless of its own setting.
THR.Rules.CriticalDice.Enabled.Name: Critical Dice: Maximize Best Dice
THR.Rules.CriticalDice.Enabled.Hint: On a critical hit, the dice with the most to gain are replaced with their maximum. Selection is by potential gain, not by lowest roll - a 5 on a d12 beats a 1 on a d4. Normal critical dice doubling is unchanged; this applies on top of it.
THR.Rules.CriticalDice.Count.Name: Critical Dice: Dice Maximized
THR.Rules.CriticalDice.Count.Hint: How many dice are maximized on each critical hit. This is the total across the whole crit, not per damage part - a Rogue's weapon dice and Sneak Attack dice compete for the same slots. Default 2.
THR.Rules.CriticalDice.ApplyToNPCs.Name: Critical Dice: Apply to NPCs
THR.Rules.CriticalDice.ApplyToNPCs.Hint: When on (default), every critical hit is upgraded, including monsters'. When off, only player-owned characters benefit.
THR.Rules.MaxHealing.Enabled.Name: Max Healing: Add a Maximize Button
THR.Rules.MaxHealing.Enabled.Hint: Adds a Maximize button to the healing roll dialog, which takes the maximum value instead of rolling. For potions drunk as an action, or any healing while Beacon of Hope is up. Only appears when everything being rolled is healing, so it can never quietly maximize damage as well.
THR.Rules.RollToBonus.Enabled.Name: Roll to Bonus: Apply Rolled Values
THR.Rules.RollToBonus.Enabled.Hint: Adds an Apply as bonus button to chat cards with a roll, turning the rolled number into a temporary bonus to AC, saves, attacks and more. For Swords Bard flourishes, Combat Inspiration, and any homebrew of the shape roll a die and add it to something for a while.
THR.Rules.RollToBonus.NoCombat: No combat is running, so turn-based durations have nothing to count from. The bonus will stay until you remove it by hand.
THR.Rules.RollToBonus.NoRecipient: No one to apply the bonus to. Select or target a token first.
THR.Rules.RollToBonus.NotOwner: You do not have permission to add effects to {name}. Ask the GM to apply it.
THR.Rules.RollToBonus.BadValue: That is not a usable bonus value.
THR.Rules.RollToBonus.Failed: Could not apply the bonus. Check the console (F12).
THR.Rules.SourceNamedEffects.Enabled.Nam: Effect Names: Use the Source Item Name
THR.Rules.SourceNamedEffects.Enabled.Hin: Names applied effects after the item that produced them, so casting Shield gives you an effect called Shield rather than Imperceptible Barrier. Conditions, concentration and enchantments keep their own names. Affects newly applied effects; use the button below to convert ones already in your world.
THR.Rules.SourceNamedEffects.Sweep.Name: Rename Existing Effects
THR.Rules.SourceNamedEffects.Sweep.Label: Rename Existing Effects
THR.Rules.SourceNamedEffects.Sweep.Hint: Rename effects already sitting on actors so they match the new naming, instead of leaving your world half converted.
THR.Rules.SourceNamedEffects.Sweep.Confi: Rename every effect in this world to match the item it came from? This edits your actors, including unlinked tokens on every scene, and cannot be undone automatically. Conditions, concentration and enchantments are left alone.
THR.Rules.SourceNamedEffects.Sweep.Done: Renamed {count} effect(s) to match their source item.
THR.Rules.SourceNamedEffects.Sweep.GMOnl: Only the GM can rename existing effects.
THR.Rules.ExpireEffects.Enabled.Name: Expire Effects: Remove Them When Time Runs Out
THR.Rules.ExpireEffects.Enabled.Hint: Nothing in Foundry or dnd5e removes an effect once its duration ends, so bonuses linger forever. This removes them when their time is up. When a concentration spell runs out, the caster stops concentrating and dnd5e removes the effect from every target.
THR.Rules.ExpireEffects.Mode.Name: Expire Effects: What To Do
THR.Rules.ExpireEffects.Mode.Hint: Whether an expired effect is deleted outright or just switched off. Disabling leaves it on the sheet so you can see what happened. Concentration is always deleted regardless, because dnd5e counts a disabled concentration marker as still concentrating, so switching one off would leave the caster silently locked into a spell that has ended.
THR.Rules.ExpireEffects.Mode.Disable: Disable it, but leave it there
THR.Rules.RollToBonus.Scope.Name: Roll to Bonus: Where The Button Appears
THR.Rules.RollToBonus.Scope.Hint: Which chat cards get an Apply as bonus button. Attack rolls never do, since a to-hit number is not a bonus anyone hands out. Bare skill checks and saving throws never do either, because they come from no item.
THR.Rules.RollToBonus.NoRoller: Could not work out who made this roll. Pick Targeted or Selected tokens instead.
